title: Maternal use of methamphetamine induces sex-dependent changes in myocardial gene expression in adult offspring.
ehr_evidence: The study utilized adult Sprague-Dawley rat offspring from pregnant dams administered methamphetamine or saline during gestation.
summary: Experimental study examining sex-dependent changes in myocardial gene expression in adult rat offspring following prenatal methamphetamine exposure.
key_findings: RNA sequencing identified 346 differentially expressed mRNAs in adult hearts.
184 changes occurred only in females, 89 only in males, and 74 were common to both sexes.
BDH1 protein expression was significantly decreased in both male (p < 0.01) and female (p < 0.05) offspring.
DDAH2 protein expression was significantly decreased in female hearts (p < 0.01) but not in male hearts.
limitations: Animal model limits direct translation to human physiology
Lack of in vivo functional cardiac outcome measures
